verses.text_en: Then he called Hermon, who had charge of the elephants. Full of rage, altogether fixed in his furious design,
verses.text_hr: Zatim je pozvao Hermona, nadstojnika slonova. Ispunjen bijesom i potpuno odlučan provesti svoj mahniti naum,

verses.text_en: he commanded him, with a quantity of unmixed wine with handfuls of incense infused, to drug the elephants early on the following day. These five hundred elephants were, when infuriated by the copious drinks of frankincense, to be led up to the execution of death upon the Jews.
verses.text_hr: zapovjedio mu je da rano sljedećega dana omami slonove obiljem nerazrijeđena vina u koje će umiješati pune pregršti tamjana. Tih pet stotina slonova, razjarene obilnim napitkom s tamjanom, trebalo je povesti da izvrše smrtnu kaznu nad Židovima.

verses.text_en: The king, after issuing these orders, went to his feasting, and gathered together all those of his friends and of the army who hated the Jews the most.
verses.text_hr: Nakon što je izdao te zapovijedi, kralj je otišao na gozbu i okupio sve svoje prijatelje i vojnike koji su najviše mrzili Židove.

verses.text_en: The master of the elephants, Hermon, fulfilled his commission punctually.
verses.text_hr: Hermon, nadstojnik slonova, točno je izvršio povjereni nalog.

verses.text_en: The servants appointed for the purpose went out about evening and bound the hands of the miserable victims, and took other precautions for their security at night, thinking that the whole race would perish together.
verses.text_hr: Sluge određene za taj posao izišle su predvečer, svezale ruke nesretnim žrtvama i poduzele druge mjere kako bi ih tijekom noći držale pod stražom, misleći da će cijeli rod zajedno izginuti.

verses.text_en: The heathen believed the Jews to be destitute of all protection, for chains bound them.
verses.text_hr: Pogani su vjerovali da su Židovi ostali bez ikakve zaštite jer su ih sputavali lanci.

verses.text_en: They invoked the Almighty Lord, and ceaselessly implored with tears their merciful God and Father, Ruler of all, Lord of every power,
verses.text_hr: Oni su zazivali svemogućega Gospodina te sa suzama bez prestanka molili svojega milosrdnog Boga i Oca, Vladara svega i Gospodara svake sile,

verses.text_en: to overthrow the evil purpose which had gone out against them, and to deliver them by extraordinary manifestation from that death which was in store for them.
verses.text_hr: da obori zli naum donesen protiv njih i izvanrednim ih očitovanjem izbavi od smrti koja ih je čekala.

verses.text_en: Their earnest entreaty went up to heaven.
verses.text_hr: Njihova se usrdna molitva uzdigla do neba.

verses.text_en: Then Hermon, who had filled his merciless elephants with copious drinks of mixed wine and frankincense, came early to the palace to report on these preparations.
verses.text_hr: Hermon je rano došao u palaču izvijestiti o pripremama, pošto je svoje nemilosrdne slonove napojio obiljem vina pomiješana s tamjanom.

verses.text_en: He, however, who has sent his good creature sleep from all time by night or by day thus gratifying whom he wills, diffused a portion of it now upon the king.
verses.text_hr: Ali Onaj koji od početka vremena noću i danju šalje dobro stvorenje sna i njime obdaruje koga hoće, upravo ga je tada spustio i na kralja.

verses.text_en: By this sweet and profound influence of the Lord, he was held fast, and thus his unjust purpose was quite frustrated, and his unflinching resolve greatly falsified.
verses.text_hr: Slatka i duboka sila Gospodnja čvrsto ga je obuzela. Tako je njegov nepravedni naum posve osujećen, a njegova nepokolebljiva odluka potpuno izjalovljena.

verses.text_en: But the Jews, having escaped the hour which had been fixed, praised their holy God, and again prayed him who is easily reconciled to display the power of his powerful hand to the arrogant Gentiles.
verses.text_hr: Židovi su, izbjegavši određeni čas, hvalili svojega svetog Boga te ponovno molili Onoga koji se lako smiluje da oholim poganima pokaže snagu svoje moćne ruke.

verses.text_en: The middle of the tenth hour had nearly arrived, when the person who sent invitations, seeing the guests who were invited present, came and shook the king.
verses.text_hr: Već se približila polovica desetoga sata kad je dvorski službenik zadužen za pozive, vidjevši da su pozvani gosti već nazočni, došao i prodrmao kralja.

verses.text_en: He gained his attention with difficulty, and hinting that the mealtime was getting past, talked the matter over with him.
verses.text_hr: Jedva mu je privukao pozornost, a zatim mu dao do znanja da vrijeme objeda prolazi i o tome s njime porazgovarao.

verses.text_en: The king listened to this, and then turning aside to his drinking, commanded the guests to sit down before him.
verses.text_hr: Kralj ga je saslušao, potom se vratio piću i naredio gostima da sjednu pred njim.

verses.text_en: This done, he asked them to enjoy themselves, and to indulge in mirth at this somewhat late hour of the banquet.
verses.text_hr: Kad su sjeli, pozvao ih je da se opuste i predaju veselju u taj već pomalo kasni sat gozbe.

verses.text_en: Conversation grew on, and the king sent for Hermon, and inquired of him, with fierce denunciations, why the Jews had been allowed to outlive that day.
verses.text_hr: Kad se razgovor razvio, kralj je pozvao Hermona i uz žestoke prijetnje upitao ga zašto je Židovima bilo dopušteno da prežive taj dan.

verses.text_en: Hermon explained that he had done his bidding over night; and in this he was confirmed by his friends.
verses.text_hr: Hermon je objasnio da je još tijekom noći učinio što mu je kralj zapovjedio, a njegovi su prijatelji to potvrdili.

verses.text_en: The king, then, with a barbarity exceeding that of Phalaris, said, “They might thank his sleep of that day. Lose no time, and get ready the elephants against tomorrow, as you did before, for the destruction of these accursed Jews.”
verses.text_hr: Tada je kralj, barbarskiji čak i od Falarida, rekao: „Za to mogu zahvaliti mojem današnjem snu. Ne gubi vrijeme, nego za sutra opet pripremi slonove kao i prije, da unište te proklete Židove.“

verses.text_en: When the king said this, the company present were glad, and approved. Then each man went to his own home.
verses.text_hr: Kad je kralj to rekao, nazočno se društvo obradovalo i odobrilo njegove riječi. Potom se svatko vratio svojemu domu.

verses.text_en: They didn’t employ the night in sleep, but in contriving cruel mockeries for those deemed miserable.
verses.text_hr: Noć nisu proveli spavajući, nego smišljajući okrutna izrugivanja onima koje su držali bijednima.

verses.text_en: The morning cock had just crowed, and Hermon, having harnessed the brutes, was stimulating them in the great colonnade.
verses.text_hr: Tek što je zapjevao jutarnji pijetao, Hermon je već upregnuo zvijeri i razdraživao ih u velikoj kolonadi.

verses.text_en: The city crowds were collected together to see the hideous spectacle, and waited impatiently for the dawn.
verses.text_hr: Gradsko se mnoštvo okupilo da vidi jeziv prizor i nestrpljivo je čekalo svitanje.

verses.text_en: The Jews, breathless with momentary suspense, stretched out their hands and prayed the Greatest God, in mournful strains, again to help them speedily.
verses.text_hr: Židovi su, bez daha u neizvjesnosti svakoga trenutka, pružali ruke i u žalobnim molitvama ponovno zaklinjali Svevišnjega Boga da im brzo pomogne.

verses.text_en: The sun’s rays were not yet shining and the king was waiting for his friends when Hermon came to him, calling him out, and saying that his desires could now be realized.
verses.text_hr: Sunčeve zrake još nisu sjale, a kralj je čekao svoje prijatelje, kad mu je Hermon pristupio, pozvao ga van i rekao da se njegove želje sada mogu ostvariti.

verses.text_en: The king, receiving him, was astonished at his unusual invitation. Overwhelmed with a spirit of oblivion about everything, inquired about the object of this earnest preparation.
verses.text_hr: Kad ga je kralj primio, začudio se njegovu neobičnom pozivu. Obuzet duhom zaborava na sve što se dogodilo, upitao je čemu služe te gorljive pripreme.

verses.text_en: But this was the working of that Almighty God who had made him forget all his purpose.
verses.text_hr: To je bilo djelo svemogućega Boga, koji je učinio da kralj zaboravi cijeli svoj naum.

verses.text_en: Hermon and all his friends pointed out the preparation of the animals. They are ready, O king, according to your own strict injunction.
verses.text_hr: Hermon i svi njegovi prijatelji pokazali su mu pripremljene životinje i rekli: „Spremne su, kralju, točno prema tvojoj strogoj zapovijedi.“

verses.text_en: The king was filled with fierce anger at these words, for, by the Providence of God regarding these things, his mind had become entirely confused. He looked hard at Hermon, and threatened him as follows:
verses.text_hr: Na te se riječi kralj razbjesnio jer mu je Božja Providnost u vezi s tim događajima potpuno pomutila um. Oštro je pogledao Hermona i ovako mu zaprijetio:

verses.text_en: “Your parents, or your children, were they here, would have given a large meal to these wild animals, not these innocent Jews, who have loyally served me and my forefathers.
verses.text_hr: „Da su ovdje tvoji roditelji ili djeca, oni bi tim divljim životinjama poslužili kao obilna gozba, a ne ovi nedužni Židovi koji su odano služili meni i mojim precima.

verses.text_en: Had it not been for familiar friendship, and the claims of your office, your life should have gone for theirs.”
verses.text_hr: Da nije našega dugogodišnjeg prijateljstva i dužnosti koju obnašaš, tvoj bi život bio dan umjesto njihovih.“

verses.text_en: Hermon, being threatened in this unexpected and alarming manner, was troubled in his eyes, and his face fell.
verses.text_hr: Hermon se uznemirio zbog te neočekivane i strašne prijetnje; pogled mu se smutio, a lice klonulo.

verses.text_en: The friends, too, stole out one by one, and dismissed the assembled multitudes to their respective occupations.
verses.text_hr: I prijatelji su se jedan po jedan neprimjetno povukli te okupljeno mnoštvo poslali natrag njegovim svakodnevnim poslovima.

verses.text_en: The Jews, having heard of these events, praised the glorious God and King of kings, because they had obtained this help, too, from him.
verses.text_hr: Kad su Židovi čuli što se dogodilo, hvalili su slavnoga Boga i Kralja kraljeva jer su i tu pomoć primili od njega.

verses.text_en: Now the king arranged another banquet in the same way, and proclaimed an invitation to mirth.
verses.text_hr: Kralj je zatim na isti način priredio novu gozbu i objavio poziv na veselje.

verses.text_en: He summoned Hermon to his presence, and said, with threats, “How often, O wretch, must I repeat my orders to you about these same persons?
verses.text_hr: Pozvao je Hermona preda se i uz prijetnje mu rekao: „Koliko ti puta, bijedniče, moram ponavljati svoje zapovijedi o tim istim ljudima?

verses.text_en: Once more, arm the elephants for the extermination of the Jews tomorrow!”
verses.text_hr: Još jednom opremi slonove da sutra istrijebe Židove!“

verses.text_en: His kinsmen, who were reclining with him, wondered at his instability, and thus expressed themselves:
verses.text_hr: Njegovi rođaci, koji su s njim bili za stolom, čudili su se njegovoj nepostojanosti te rekli:

verses.text_en: “O king, how long do you test us, as of men bereft of reason? This is the third time that you have ordered their destruction. When the thing is to be done, you change your mind, and recall your instructions.
verses.text_hr: „Kralju, koliko ćeš nas još iskušavati kao da smo ljudi lišeni razuma? Ovo je već treći put da zapovijedaš njihovo uništenje. A kad treba izvršiti nalog, predomisliš se i opozoveš svoje upute.

verses.text_en: Because of this, the feeling of expectation causes tumult in the city. It swarms with factions, and is continually on the point of being plundered.”
verses.text_hr: Zbog toga iščekivanje izaziva nemir u gradu. Grad vrvi sukobljenim skupinama i neprestano mu prijeti pljačka.“

verses.text_en: The king, just like another Phalaris, a prey to thoughtlessness, made no account of the changes which his own mind had undergone, issuing in the deliverance of the Jews. He swore a fruitless oath, and determined immediately to send them to hades, crushed by the knees and feet of the elephants.
verses.text_hr: Kralj, posve nalik drugom Falaridu i prepušten nepromišljenosti, uopće nije uzimao u obzir promjene vlastita uma koje su dovele do izbavljenja Židova. Zakleo se ispraznom zakletvom i odlučio da ih odmah pošalje u Had, zgnječene koljenima i nogama slonova.

verses.text_en: He would also invade Judea, level its towns with fire and the sword, destroy that temple which the heathen might not enter, and prevent sacrifices ever after being offered up there.
verses.text_hr: Namjeravao je upasti i u Judeju, ognjem i mačem sravniti njezine gradove, razoriti Hram u koji pogani nisu smjeli ulaziti te zauvijek spriječiti prinošenje žrtava na tom mjestu.

verses.text_en: Joyfully his friends broke up, together with his kinsmen; and, trusting in his determination, arranged their forces in guard at the most convenient places of the city.
verses.text_hr: Njegovi prijatelji i rođaci radosno su se razišli. Uzdajući se u njegovu odlučnost, rasporedili su svoje snage kao stražu na najprikladnijim mjestima u gradu.

verses.text_en: The master of the elephants urged the animals into an almost maniacal state, drenched them with incense and wine, and decked them with frightful devices.
verses.text_hr: Nadstojnik slonova dotjerao je životinje gotovo do ludila: obilno ih je napojio vinom i tamjanom te okitio zastrašujućom opremom.

verses.text_en: About early morning, when the city was filled with an immense number of people at the hippodrome, he entered the palace and called the king to the business in hand.
verses.text_hr: U rano jutro, kad se u gradu oko hipodroma okupilo neizmjerno mnoštvo, ušao je u palaču i pozvao kralja da pristupi izvršenju nauma.

verses.text_en: The king’s heart teemed with impious rage; and he rushed forth with the mass, along with the elephants. With unsoftened feelings and pitiless eyes, he longed to gaze at the hard and wretched doom of the previously mentioned Jews.
verses.text_hr: Kraljevo je srce kipjelo od bezbožna bijesa. Izjurio je s mnoštvom i slonovima; neumoljiva srca i nemilosrdna pogleda žudio je promatrati tešku i bijednu sudbinu već spomenutih Židova.

verses.text_en: But the Jews, when the elephants went out at the gate, followed by the armed force. When they saw the dust raised by the throng, and heard the loud cries of the crowd,
verses.text_hr: Kad su Židovi ugledali slonove kako izlaze kroz vrata, praćene naoružanim snagama, te vidjeli prašinu koju je podiglo mnoštvo i čuli glasne povike okupljenih,

verses.text_en: thought that they had come to the last moment of their lives, to the end of what they had tremblingly expected. They gave way, therefore, to lamentations and moans. They kissed each other. Those nearest of kin to each other hung around one another’s necks—fathers hugging their sons and mothers their daughters. Other women held their infants to their breasts, which drew what seemed their last milk.
verses.text_hr: pomislili su da je došao posljednji trenutak njihova života i kraj onoga što su sa strepnjom iščekivali. Prepustili su se naricanju i jecajima. Ljubili su jedni druge, a najbliži rođaci grlili su se oko vrata — očevi sinove, majke kćeri. Druge su žene na prsima držale dojenčad koja je sisala, kako se činilo, posljednje mlijeko.

verses.text_en: Nevertheless, when they reflected upon the help previously granted them from heaven, they prostrated themselves with one accord, removed even the sucking children from the breasts, and
verses.text_hr: Ipak, kad su se prisjetili pomoći koju su već primili s neba, jednodušno su se bacili ničice, odvojili čak i dojenčad od prsa

verses.text_en: sent up an exceedingly great cry asking the Lord of all power to reveal himself, and have mercy upon those who now lay at the gates of hades.
verses.text_hr: te podigli silan vapaj, moleći Gospodara svake sile da se objavi i smiluje onima koji sada leže na vratima Hada.
